_comment: Sourced distance findings from doctrine.md §2, overlaid on the coarse echelon bands in bands.json rather than replacing them. bands.json stays as the four broad echelon bands the master prompt specified; these markers are the narrower, individually-sourced depth patterns, shown as an optional ruler overlay. Side attribution follows the representative-equipment convention used throughout the tool (side_a = the side whose examples are Western-supplied systems, side_b = the side whose examples are Russian systems); where a source is side-agnostic, side is 'both'.

markers.label: Radio FPV strike envelope
markers.note: Standard radio-link FPV combat radius without a relay — the older, still-common baseline. Fiber-optic FPVs go well beyond this; see the separate marker.

markers.label: Fiber-optic FPV envelope
markers.note: Jam-proof tethered FPVs now field at ~20 km as a practical working range on both sides (cable strength is the limit, not signal). Extended coils are already fielded well beyond that — reported up to 50 km (Ukraine's Ptashka, and separately Russian systems) and a claimed 65 km test spool — reaching well past the old radio-FPV envelope and into rear logistics and even cities behind the line.

markers.label: Close reconnaissance
markers.note: The 'second line' — activated within seconds of a detection.

markers.label: Forward command post
markers.note: Forward CP at 2–5 km; the combat trains CP sits roughly 10 km further back.

markers.label: Drone-dense corridor
markers.note: ~30 km either side of the ~1,200 km front — the zone where persistent drone coverage genuinely dominates.

markers.label: FPV launch teams
markers.note: Launch teams 8–10 km back; control and relay equipment a further ~10 km behind them (~20 km total).

markers.label: Medium / long-range strike & recon
markers.note: Deep-strike layer; some platforms fly autonomously along pre-planned routes.

markers.label: Offensive staging areas
markers.note: Movement forward split into guided segments over 3–4 days, radio silence, paper orders only.

lower_sky_control._comment: doctrine.md §2's sharpest finding, kept as data so the planned interactive toggle reads from config rather than hardcoded numbers. Not yet wired to an interactive control — see docs/DECISIONS.md.
lower_sky_control.finding: Local air/drone superiority — not doctrine or preference — sets how close you can position assets.

without_control.note: Pushed back to roughly 7 km and restricted to indirect fire.
